title: A&R work for Lauderdale's company and Jesse Belvin
summary: He was A&R man, arranger and contractor for the small label, and was first to record Jesse Belvin; he mentions again passing on "Night Train".

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Then in later years I made many records with Bumps, because I was an A&R man for Dolphin's of Hollywood during one period, and we used to record every single day. I was the first to record Jesse Belvin, for instance. I used to do all the arranging and all the contracting and all the producing for that little company. Later, when I remember the name of the company, I'll insert it somewhere, but it was Jack Lauderdale's company who Lloyd Glenn was a star with. So Jack hired me to be an A&R man... Did I tell this one, when we went up to St. Louis...?
To hear Jimmy Forrest. I told this one already.
And Jack didn't buy "Night Train," so the rest is history.
